items.slide_topic: Inside the model: what a 'feature' is
items.dek: In the “mind” of Claude, we found millions of concepts that activate when the model reads relevant text or sees relevant images, which we call “features”. One of those was the concept of the Golden Gate Bridge.
items.caption: Anthropic's own definition of a 'feature' from the Golden Gate Claude announcement.
items.notes: Copied verbatim from the page text (curl of the page). The first sentence is the definition; the second is the page's example.

items.slide_topic: Inside the model: turning a feature up changes behavior
items.dek: For instance, we see that clamping the Golden Gate Bridge feature 34M/31164353 to 10× its maximum activation value induces thematically-related model behavior. In this example, the model starts to self-identify as the Golden Gate Bridge!
items.caption: The paper's description of steering: pinning the bridge feature to 10x its maximum makes the model start to self-identify as the bridge.
items.notes: Copied verbatim from the paper's 'Influence on Behavior' section (curl of the page). 'Clamping' means forcing the feature to a fixed high or low value during the forward pass.

items.slide_topic: Golden Gate Claude: an example of what it said
items.dek: Golden Gate - This iconic bridge name would be a fitting moniker for the pelican with its striking orange color and beautiful suspension cables.
items.caption: A real reply from Golden Gate Claude, quoted in a May 24, 2024 blog post: the user asked for names for a pet pelican.
items.notes: Secondary source quoting the demo, verified verbatim by curl of the post. The same post also quotes the pretzel-recipe reply: 'Gently wipe any fog away and pour the warm chocolate mixture over the bridge/brick combination.' Post also says: 'No matter what question you ask it the Golden Gate Bridge is likely to be involved in the answer in some way.'

datasets.title: Sparse autoencoder sizes trained on Claude 3 Sonnet (number of features)
datasets.source: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity (2024-05-21), training section: 'We trained three SAEs of varying sizes: 1,048,576 (~1M), 4,194,304 (~4M), and 33,554,432 (~34M) features.'

datasets.title: Dead features by SAE size (paper says 'roughly')
datasets.source: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity (2024-05-21): 'dead' features are those not active over a sample of 10^7 tokens; 'The proportion of dead features was roughly 2% for the 1M SAE, 35% for the 4M SAE, and 65% for the 34M SAE.'

facts.claim: Anthropic released Golden Gate Claude as a research demo dated May 23, 2024; it was online for a 24-hour period and is no longer available.

Anthropic says that when it turned up the strength of the 'Golden Gate Bridge' feature, Claude's responses began to focus on the bridge: 'Its replies to most queries start to mention the Golden Gate Bridge, even if it's not directly relevant.'
Anthropic's 'Scaling Monosemanticity' paper (published May 21, 2024) extracted features from Claude 3 Sonnet, the 3.0 version: 'released March 4, 2024'.
The paper's authors say they found 'millions of features' and that 'Scaling feature exploration is an important open problem ... which we do not solve in this paper.'
'The resulting features are highly abstract: multilingual, multimodal, and generalizing between concrete and abstract references.' (paper's key results)
facts.source: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity (Transformer Circuits Thread), Key Results

facts.claim: The features also activate on images, even though the dictionary learning was run only on text: 'Note that these features also activate on relevant images, despite our only performing dictionary learning on a text-based dataset!'
The paper reports features related to a broad range of safety concerns, including deception, sycophancy, bias, and dangerous content.
facts.source: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity (Transformer Circuits Thread), Key Results

facts.claim: The Golden Gate Bridge feature (34M/31164353): 'Its greatest activations are essentially all references to the bridge, and weaker activations also include related tourist attractions, similar bridges, and other monuments.'
Plain-words version of the paper's definition: a 'feature' is one concept inside the AI's network, such as the Golden Gate Bridge, that lights up when the model reads text or sees images about it.
facts.source: Paraphrase of Anthropic's definition: 'millions of concepts that activate when the model reads relevant text or sees relevant images, which we call features' (Golden Gate Claude page)

facts.claim: Anthropic trained three sparse autoencoders with 1,048,576 (~1M), 4,194,304 (~4M), and 33,554,432 (~34M) features; the largest had roughly 65% dead features versus roughly 2% for the 1M one.
facts.source: Anthropic, Scaling Monosemanticity (Transformer Circuits Thread), Methodological Details
